artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}$ with $|A|=n$, and let $G \subseteq A\times A$. Define the partial sumset and partial difference set along $G$ by
$$A\stackrel{G}{+}A := \{a'+a'' : (a',a'')\in G\}, \qquad A\stackrel{G}{-}A := \{a'-a'' : (a',a'')\in G\}.$$
The problem is to obtain an upper bound on $|A\stackrel{G}{-}A|$ in terms of $|A\stackrel{G}{+}A|$ and $n$, and to characterize the finite sets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ (together with the choice of $G$) for which $|A\stackrel{G}{-}A|$ attains the maximum possible value.

It is known that:
(i) if $|A\stackrel{G}{+}A|=1$, then $|A\stackrel{G}{-}A|\le n$, with equality only when $A$ is symmetric (i.e. $A=c-A$ for some $c\in\mathbb{Z}$);
(ii) if $|A\stackrel{G}{+}A|=2$, then $|A\stackrel{G}{-}A|\le 2n-1$, with equality only when $A$ is an arithmetic progression.

Provide the analogous sharp bound and extremal characterization for general values of $|A\stackrel{G}{+}A|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question by G. Freiman in a compilation of open problems in additive combinatorics. Only the cases $|A\stackrel{G}{+}A|\le 3$ are reported as fully solved, and no general sharp bound for arbitrary $|A\stackrel{G}{+}A|$ appears in the literature.
